title: Rounding to the nearest thousand
canonical_examples_source: Number-line rounding method + round-half-up convention: NCERT Class 5 Maths (Maths Mela, large numbers) and Illustrative Mathematics Grade 5 (rounding on the number line); format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths. Arithmetic self-verified.

blocks.content: Maya is counting the beads in a big jar. She counts 8,214 beads! That is a hard number to say out loud, so we round it — we swap it for a close, tidy number. Rounding to the nearest thousand asks one thing: which thousand is the number closest to? Quick words: digit means a single number symbol like 0, 1, 2 up to 9. round means swap a number for a close, tidier one.
Every number sits between two thousands. To round to the nearest thousand, find those two thousands, then pick the one the number is CLOSER to.

blocks.question: Look at the dot for 6,432. Which thousand is it closer to? Tap to check.
blocks.content: 6,432 comes before the halfway mark (6,500), so it is closer to 6,000. It rounds to 6,000.
4,500 sits EXACTLY on the halfway line — the same distance from both thousands. That is called a tie. Everyone agrees on one rule: a number exactly halfway rounds UP. So 4,500 rounds to 5,000.

blocks.prompt: The halfway mark between 4,000 and 5,000 is ___.
blocks.explain: Halfway between 4,000 and 5,000 is 4,500. Numbers below it round down to 4,000; 4,500 and above round up to 5,000.
blocks.rule: Compare the number to the halfway mark: below it rounds down, at or above it rounds up.

blocks.content: You do not have to draw the line every time. To know which side of halfway you are on, look at the digit JUST TO THE RIGHT of the place you are rounding. For the nearest thousand that is the hundreds digit: 0 to 4 is below halfway (round down), 5 to 9 is halfway or above (round up). The same idea rounds to any place — nearest ten? look at the ones; nearest hundred? look at the tens.

blocks.question: Round 8,512 to the nearest thousand.
blocks.explain: The digit right of the thousands is the hundreds digit, 5. A 5 means 8,512 is at or past the 8,500 halfway mark, so it is closer to 9,000. It rounds to 9,000.
blocks.rule: To round to the nearest thousand, check the hundreds digit: 5 to 9 rounds up, 0 to 4 rounds down.

practiceItems.prompt: the place you check when rounding to the nearest thousand

blocks.question: Now round 6,432 to the nearest HUNDRED instead. Sian says to check the hundreds digit again. Which digit should she really check, and what is the answer?
options: The tens digit (3) — it is just right of the hundreds place; 3 is under 5, so 6,400
The hundreds digit (4), so the answer is 6,000
You cannot round to the nearest hundred
blocks.explain: The rule is always the same: look at the digit just to the RIGHT of the place you are rounding to. For the nearest hundred, that is the tens digit. In 6,432 the tens digit is 3, which is under 5, so it rounds down to 6,400. The hundreds digit is only for rounding to the nearest thousand.
blocks.rule: To round to ANY place, look at the digit immediately to the right of that place.
blocks.principle: The digit you check is always the one just to the right of the place you are rounding to; the same idea works for tens, hundreds and thousands.
canonical_solution: Rounding to the nearest hundred, the rounding place is the hundreds
Check the digit just to its right: the tens digit
3 is under 5, so round down to 6,400

rubric.look_for: identifies the digit just right of the rounding place (the tens)
uses the tens digit 3 to round to 6,400, not 6,000
states the general rule — check the digit just right of the place

misconceptions.coach: The hundreds digit is only for the nearest thousand. Check the digit just right of whatever place you are rounding to.
That is rounding to the nearest thousand. For the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit.

practiceItems.prompt: to round to the nearest ten, which digit do you check?
to round to the nearest hundred, which digit do you check?

blocks.content: So rounding is really one idea: which mark is the number closest to, with a halfway tie going up. The shortcut — check the digit just right of the place you are rounding — works for tens, hundreds and thousands alike. Let's practise!
